title: Team Members Who Excel Most at Managing UP
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece distinguishes healthy self-advocacy from manipulative self-promotion at work. Team members who quietly ensure a leader knows about their contributions are managing up in a legitimate, career-sustaining way, since leaders can't reward work they never hear about. The piece draws a firm line at the point where self-promotion crosses into obsequious flattery divorced from real results, which peers recognize and resent. Left unchecked, that dynamic corrodes morale as genuine contributors watch shallow self-promoters get credit they haven't earned. The archivist reads this as a caution to leaders: verify contributions independently rather than relying solely on what people report about themselves.
points: Leaders can only reward what they know about, which makes some degree of self-promotion a rational survival strategy for team members, not a character flaw by default.
The dividing line between managing up and kissing up is whether the self-promotion is backed by actual delivered results.
Unchecked flattery without substance breeds cynicism among high performers who watch credit flow to people who didn't earn it through output.
Good leaders counteract this by independently verifying who is actually driving outcomes rather than trusting self-reported contributions at face value.
quotes: Leaders who don’t know about the efforts a team member makes on their behalf can’t reward them for their good work.
When a team member goes too far in this self-promotion and makes it clear they stand ready to help the leader in any way they can, they are thought to be kissing up rather than managing up.
But it becomes a much bigger problem when those who excel at kissing up don’t actually get the job done or create the results they tout.
The disparaging commentary between teammates about this “brown noser” can undermine team morale and create a negative team atmosphere.
Over time, they fall prey to cynicism and despair. Getting ahead, it now seems, has little to do with producing great work but everything to do with managing and kissing up.
They don’t depend on what team members tell them or allow the charms of self-promotion to color their view. They distinguish between words and deeds.
